# STLACCESS — My STL Scale Converter for 3D Printed Miniatures

&gt; I built this browser-based tool suite to calculate resize percentages for scaling STL files between tabletop gaming systems. It's free, requires no upload, and needs no login. All the math runs in your browser. I built it with Astro. The brand is **STLACCESS** — "STL scale" always refers to the *function* (scaling STL files), never to a product name.

## What I built STLACCESS for

I built STLACCESS to solve one problem I kept hitting: figuring out what percentage to type into my slicer to scale an STL file from one miniature scale to another. Every conversion I publish uses a 175cm human baseline, measured to eye level (160cm) by default. The site hosts the main **STL Scale Engine** (the calculator on the homepage), a reference library of 46 verified conversions, 26 game-system guides, 6 deep-dive guides, and supporting tools for 3D printing hobbyists like me.

## How I calculate every conversion

- **Human baseline:** 175cm (5'9"). **Eyes at 160cm.**
- **Gaming/display scales** (28mm, 32mm, 35mm, 40mm, 75mm, 6mm, 8mm, 10mm, 30mm, 15mm) are measured to **eye level**.
- **Ratio scales** (1:35, 1:27, 1:48, 1:56, 1:72, 1:100) are measured to the **top of the head**.
- **Formula I use:** `(target standard mm ÷ source standard mm) × 100 = slicer percentage`.

Canonical examples I verify on my own prints: 28mm → 32mm = **114.3%** (top-of-head variant 116.1%); 32mm → 28mm = **87.5%**;
1:35 → 1:56 = **62.5%**; 1:100 → 28mm = **160.0%**; 32mm → 75mm = **234.4%**.
The eye-to-top-of-head gap (~15cm) creates a **5–10%** difference in calculated scale.

## Key pages I built

- [STL Scale Converter (homepage)](https://stlaccess.com/) — Main calculator (the STL Scale Engine): 16 tabletop scales, eye-level and top-of-head measurement, shrinkage compensation toggle, copy-to-clipboard, deep-linkable URL params
- [Scale Conversion Reference](https://stlaccess.com/reference) — 46 verified conversion percentages with my math breakdowns, print-tested results, and community feedback system
- [Conversion FAQ](https://stlaccess.com/faq) — Answers I wrote about 28mm, 32mm, 35mm, 1:35, 1:48, 1:56, 1:72, and 1:100 scales
- [Methodology / About](https://stlaccess.com/about) — My 175cm human baseline, FDM test prints with a PARKSIDE digital caliper, and the story behind why I started this project
- [All Tools](https://stlaccess.com/tools) — STL Scale Engine, Scale Conversion Reference, Slicer Percentage Calculator, Filament Cost Calculator, Real-World to Miniature Scale Converter, STL Scale Reference Bar Generator, and Miniature Scale Identifier
- [Game Systems](https://stlaccess.com/games) — Scale guides I wrote for 26 tabletop games with related conversions, printing tips, and base sizes
- [Guides](https://stlaccess.com/guides) — 6 deep-dive guides I wrote on miniature scale, 3D printing, and conversion math
- [Slicer Percentage Calculator](https://stlaccess.com/tools/slicer-percentage-calculator) — Enter any current height and target height to get the exact slicer percentage
- [Filament Cost Calculator](https://stlaccess.com/tools/filament-cost-calculator) — Calculate print cost from filament price, weight, and optional electricity
- [Miniature Scale Identifier](https://stlaccess.com/tools/miniature-scale-identifier) — Measure a model's height in mm (slicer bounding box or ruler) and it tells you which scale it matches — 28mm, 32mm heroic, 35mm Legion, 40mm Shatterpoint, 1:35 kits, and more — with matched game systems and a deep-link into the engine
- [Real-World to Miniature Scale Converter](https://stlaccess.com/tools/real-world-scale-converter) — Reverse of the engine: convert real-world measurements (feet/inches) to exact mm at any tabletop scale
- [STL Scale Reference Bar Generator](https://stlaccess.com/tools/reference-bar-generator) — Generate a download-and-print STL ruler bar (5mm ticks + end tab the exact height of a figure at that scale) to calibrate in Lychee or Chitubox
- [Privacy Policy](https://stlaccess.com/privacy) — No cookies, no personal data collection. Cookie-free analytics only.
- [Terms](https://stlaccess.com/terms) — Terms of use

- [Contact](https://stlaccess.com/contact) — Report errors, request new scales, suggest features

## Guides I wrote (6 total)

Every guide I write opens with a **Direct Answer box** (rendered from frontmatter `tldr`) plus jump links to its sections. `description` is used for SEO/meta only. Game-specific guides (Warhammer 40k, Bolt Action, D&D) were merged as "Deep Dive" sections of /games, and the chart + 28mm→32mm guides were merged into /reference — all five old URLs 301-redirect.

- [How to Measure a Miniature's Scale: Eye Level vs Top of Head Explained](https://stlaccess.com/guides/how-to-measure-miniature-scale) — Measure foot to eye level, not top of head; a "28mm" mini is ~31–32mm to the crown
- [FDM Miniature Printing: Complete Guide to Layer Height, Nozzles, and Settings](https://stlaccess.com/guides/fdm-miniature-printing-guide) — 0.2mm nozzle @ 0.06mm for characters; 0.4mm @ 0.08mm for rank-and-file; PLA, 100% fan, tilt 15–20°, tree supports
- [How to Scale Real-World Objects to 32mm Miniatures (The Math Explained)](https://stlaccess.com/guides/real-world-objects-to-32mm) — (real inches ÷ 72) × 32 = mm; an 18-ft dragon ≈ 96mm
- [Upscaling 3D Prints: How Big Can You Go Before You Lose Detail?](https://stlaccess.com/guides/upscaling-3d-prints-detail-limit) — FDM: ~50mm (156%) practical ceiling; 0.2mm nozzle at 0.08mm layers pushes it to ~80mm
- [How to Scale Miniatures in Chitubox & Lychee Slicer (Without Messing Up the Base)](https://stlaccess.com/guides/chitubox-lychee-scaling-guide) — Lock the chain-link/aspect ratio first; inch-exported files scale up 2540%
- [Why Miniature Scales Use a 175cm Human Baseline](https://stlaccess.com/guides/175cm-baseline) — Origin and reasoning behind the 175cm reference height

## How I designed the calculator

1. I select a source scale (e.g. 28mm) and target scale (e.g. 32mm)
2. The calculator divides the target standard mm by the source standard mm to get a percentage
3. I enter that percentage in my slicer (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Chitubox, Lychee, Bambu Studio)
4. The STL scales proportionally in the slicer

Formula I use: `(target standard mm) / (source standard mm) * 100 = percentage`

For ratio scales, the calculator converts ratio-to-mm using the 175cm baseline (top-of-head), then divides as normal. Gaming scales use eye-level mm.

## How I test every conversion

- Human baseline: 175cm (standard reference height used by most miniature manufacturers)
- Eye level: 160cm (default measurement method for fantasy and sci-fi)
- Top of head: 175cm (used for historical kits, display busts, and ratio scales)
- All percentages verified with FDM test prints on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini
- PARKSIDE digital caliper measurements at 0.01mm resolution (0–150mm range, all-metal construction)
- FDM accuracy: over-extrusion can add 0.3%-0.5% to dimensions
- Thermal shrinkage: PLA and PETG shrink 0.2%-0.5% during cooling (not compensated, tends to cancel with over-extrusion)
- Layer height bias: 0.1-0.2mm stair-step error on curved surfaces at 0.08mm layers

## How I built the site

- Built with Astro 7.1.3, Tailwind CSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`), TypeScript, content collections
- Static site generation (no backend, no database)
- All calculations run client-side in JavaScript
- No cookies, no accounts. Cookie-free analytics (Umami) for anonymous pageview counts only.
- Sitemap + RSS feed generated at build time
- Structured data in `src/data/*.json`; guide articles in `src/content/guides/*.md`
- Source on GitHub (kitsorix-official)

## FAQ topics I cover

- **Methodology**: Measurement methods, scale inconsistency between manufacturers, checking scale without printing
- **Sci-fi and fantasy**: Primaris vs Firstborn scale, mixing scales between systems, 28mm vs 32mm differences
- **Historical and vehicles**: 1:56 vehicle compatibility with 28mm infantry, 1:48 kits, converting 1:35 STLs to 1:56
- **FDM printing and slicers**: Bounding box height vs eye-level, filament shrinkage, FDM capability at 28mm/32mm, which slicer to use

## My editing conventions

- **Brand:** always STLACCESS. The calculator is called the STL Scale Engine / STL scale calculator — a *function*, never a brand. Never write "stlscale" as a word that looks like a product name.
- **Meta titles:** keyword-first → problem/intent → brand. Pattern: `"&lt;Keyword&gt; | &lt;intent&gt; | STLACCESS"`.
- **Meta descriptions:** ≤155 characters, natural language, name what the user gets + the problem solved.
- **Guide frontmatter:** `tldr` is the Direct Answer shown in the orange box — one punchy sentence with the key number inline. `description` stays for SEO.
- **Numbers:** always derive from the 175cm/160cm baseline and the formula above. Any change must be verified against `scales.json` / `conversions.json` / `gameSystems.json`.
- **Voice:** first-person hobbyist ("I printed it myself"), plain English.
- **Build check:** `npm run build` must stay green.

## What I've been working on

- **Scale Identifier tool** — new `/tools/miniature-scale-identifier` page that reverse-engineers a model's scale from a height measurement (eye level, top of head, or "not sure"), compares against the same 16 scale baselines with a strong-match threshold (≤12% deviation), lists matched game systems, and deep-links into the engine pre-filled. Ships with a height→scale lookup table, 3-step measuring walkthrough, and a 6-question FAQ (FAQPage JSON-LD).
- **Guide redesign** — I added Direct Answer boxes with jump-to-section navigation, reading time, H1-first reading order, restyled `.prose` (card-style tables, accent-bar headings, custom list markers).
- **SEO pass** — keyword-first titles, all 26 game meta descriptions rewritten to ≤155 characters, homepage H1 names the tool ("The STL scale calculator…"), reference hub title gained the `| STLACCESS` suffix, 4 guide descriptions trimmed, 2 tool descriptions enriched.
- **Layout & navigation** — sticky desktop nav, mobile bottom nav, breadcrumbs, skip link, H1s moved into the masthead.
- **Branding cleanup** — removed `stlscale` as a site alternate name and as a tool name; the brand is exclusively **STLACCESS**; the calculator is referred to only as the STL Scale Engine.

## About me

STLACCESS is a free, independent project I built. All percentages are calculated from a 175cm human baseline and verified with FDM test prints and digital calipers on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini. The site has no backend, no cookies, no accounts — just cookie-free analytics (Umami) for anonymous pageview stats. Everything runs in your browser. Source code is on GitHub. I started this project from frustration with scale creep in my own tabletop gaming, plus lessons I learned from a failed local print service I ran in Enschede, Netherlands.
